key_takeaways: Two-tier market: PM-JAY rates anchor mass care; a smaller paying and international segment sustains premium care.{{health_system.financing:7}}{{health_system.public_system:4}}
Mount Sinai's exclusive Ramaiah collaboration, reportedly 10 years, is CSI's closest peer model.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:19}}{{health_system.competitive_landscape:21}}
Private chains are the likeliest commercial partners; state governments are often the counterparty.{{health_system.private_system:12}}{{country_overview.government:6}}
Workforce training, from nursing to leadership, is one of the clearest openings.{{health_system.workforce:1}}{{health_system.workforce:4}}
health_system: States run delivery, from 1,81,873 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs to AIIMS and Tata Memorial Centre.{{country_overview.government:1}}{{health_system.public_system:1}}
Government health spending was 1.48% of GDP in 2022-23, short of the 2.5% target.{{health_system.financing:1}}{{health_system.financing:9}}
Under one registered doctor and 0.6 public beds per 1,000; rural centers lacked 79.9% of specialists in 2023.{{health_system.workforce:1}}{{health_system.workforce:6}}{{health_system.workforce:15}}
market: Manipal (13,037 licensed beds), Apollo (10,970, including overseas) and Aster DM Quality Care (over 10,600) lead.{{health_system.private_system:2}}{{health_system.private_system:4}}{{health_system.private_system:7}}

Capital: Manipal's Rs 9,275 crore IPO, Blackstone in Aster, KKR's pending Medicover deal, IHH controlling Fortis.{{recent_developments.4:1}}{{health_system.private_system:6}}{{health_system.private_system:14}}{{health_system.private_system:11}}
Cleveland Clinic anchors Navi Mumbai MediCity under an MoU; Mayo advises Adani's two Health Cities.{{health_system.outlook:3}}{{health_system.outlook:4}}
competitor_note: US ties are mostly advisory, network or education deals, not ownership; several are less visible than headlines suggest.
opportunities: Nursing, fellowship and allied-health training, backing budget plans for 1 lakh more allied health professionals.{{health_system.workforce:4}}{{health_system.workforce:11}}
Affiliations, second-opinion services and clinical program development with corporate hospital chains.{{health_system.private_system:2}}{{health_system.private_system:12}}

Cardiology, oncology, metabolic and transplant care in the aging south, west and National Capital Region.{{country_overview.demographics:6}}{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:1}}{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:13}}
risks: Medical arrivals fell from 6.97 lakh in 2019 to 6.44 lakh in 2024; Bangladesh, the top source, faced visa limits.{{health_system.outlook:5}}{{health_system.outlook:7}}
A 2026 US law allows tariffs up to 100% on the largest Russian energy buyers; generics face Section 232 review.{{country_overview.economy:10}}{{country_overview.economy:8}}
Thin public funding and staffing; PM-JAY tariffs set the price floor for private partners.{{health_system.outlook:12}}{{health_system.workforce:15}}{{health_system.public_system:4}}

country_background: India, with about 1.46 billion people in 2025, is a federal parliamentary democratic republic with its capital in New Delhi.{{country_overview.demographics:1}}{{country_overview.demographics:12}}{{country_overview.demographics:18}} President Droupadi Murmu is head of state, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in office since 2014, began a third term in June 2024.{{country_overview.demographics:13}}{{country_overview.demographics:16}} Health care delivery is a state responsibility under the Constitution, and a state government is often the counterparty for a foreign partner.{{country_overview.government:1}}{{country_overview.government:6}} The IMF counts India among the fastest-growing major economies: official provisional estimates put real GDP growth at 7.7 percent in FY2025-26, and the World Bank puts 2025 GDP at about US$17.2 trillion in purchasing-power terms.{{country_overview.economy:14}}{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:3}} The population is aging: fertility fell to 1.9 in 2024, below replacement, and UNFPA projects the share aged 60 and over to rise from 10.5 percent in 2022 to 20.8 percent by 2050.{{country_overview.demographics:3}}{{country_overview.demographics:6}}{{country_overview.demographics:7}} US trade policy is a risk: most Indian goods have faced a 10 percent US duty since 24 July 2026.{{country_overview.economy:6}}{{country_overview.economy:7}}
